# Counting Holomorphic Rational Curves via Mirror Symmetry in a Calabi-Yau Threefold with Discrete Torsion

This study employs the powerful framework of mirror symmetry to enumerate holomorphic rational curves in a Calabi-Yau threefold X. The particular threefold under investigation is distinguished by two notable features: it possesses Z₃ × Z₃ Wilson lines and, crucially, contains torsion curves within its homology group. These characteristics make X an especially rich setting in which to explore the interplay between geometry, topology, and the enumerative predictions of mirror symmetry.

To carry out the curve-counting program, the authors compute instanton numbers using the B-model formulated on the mirror of X, as well as on its covering spaces. This dual approach allows the enumerative invariants to be extracted systematically and cross-checked across related geometries, thereby lending robustness to the resulting computations.

A central result of the analysis is that the threefold X is self-mirror, and remarkably this property persists even at the quantum level. This self-mirror structure is not merely an elegant symmetry but a practical computational tool: it is exploited by the authors to derive the complete prepotential of the theory, providing a full description of the relevant enumerative data.

The significance of this work extends beyond the specific example it treats. Most notably, it furnishes the first known instance in which the instanton number depends on the torsion part of a curve's homology class. This observation is conceptually important, as it demonstrates that torsion, often regarded as a subtle or secondary feature of homology, can have direct and measurable consequences for enumerative invariants.

Finally, the threefold X provides a valuable non-toric example in support of the conjectured exchange of torsion subgroups between mirror manifolds. Because much of the existing evidence for such conjectures arises from toric constructions, the presence of a non-toric example strengthens the case for the general validity of this proposed relationship, and highlights X as an instructive testing ground for deeper questions in mirror symmetry.

# Mirror Symmetry and Torsion-Dependent Instanton Numbers on a Self-Mirror Calabi-Yau Threefold

## Introduction and Motivation

Mirror symmetry has long served as one of the most powerful tools in the study of Calabi-Yau geometry, allowing difficult enumerative problems on one manifold to be translated into tractable computations on its mirror partner. In its classical formulation, the mirror map exchanges the complexified Kähler moduli of a Calabi-Yau threefold X with the complex structure moduli of its mirror. The B-model, defined on the mirror manifold, encodes the Gromov-Witten invariants of X through the structure of its prepotential, from which one can extract the instanton numbers that count holomorphic rational curves. While this program has been extensively developed for simply-connected Calabi-Yau manifolds, the situation becomes considerably richer—and more subtle—when the threefold in question possesses nontrivial torsion in its integral homology.

In this work, we investigate a Calabi-Yau threefold X carrying a Z₃ × Z₃ group of Wilson lines and, correspondingly, torsion in its homology group. The presence of this torsion introduces a new degree of freedom into the enumerative problem: a curve class is now specified not only by its degree in the free part of the second homology, but also by a discrete label taking values in the torsion subgroup. The central question we address is whether the instanton numbers—the counts of holomorphic rational curves—can genuinely depend on this torsion component of the homology class.

## The B-Model Computation

To answer this question, we employ mirror symmetry and carry out the full B-model computation on the mirror of X. The essential steps are as follows. We first identify the mirror manifold and its complex structure moduli space, taking care to track the discrete data associated with the torsion. We then compute the periods of the holomorphic three-form, which satisfy a system of Picard-Fuchs differential equations. By solving these equations near the point of maximal unipotent monodromy and constructing the mirror map, we transport the B-model data into the A-model language of Kähler parameters on X.

From the periods we assemble the complete prepotential, the generating function whose instanton expansion encodes the Gromov-Witten invariants. Extracting the instanton numbers order by order, we count the holomorphic rational curves in each homology class, now organized according to both their degree and their torsion label.

## The Key Result: Torsion-Dependent Instanton Numbers

The outcome of this computation is striking. We find that the instanton numbers genuinely depend on the torsion part of a curve's homology class. To our knowledge, this constitutes the first explicit example in which such a dependence is exhibited. Curves whose homology classes differ only in their torsion component—that is, curves that agree in the free part of H₂—are counted differently. This demonstrates that the torsion subgroup is not merely a passive bookkeeping device but carries real enumerative content, refining the classical picture in which only the free part of homology was thought to govern curve counting.

## Quantum Self-Mirror Property and Torsion Exchange

Beyond the enumerative statement, our results have significant implications for the structure of mirror symmetry itself. By comparing the A-model and B-model data, we establish that X is self-mirror at the quantum level: the quantum-corrected geometry of X is isomorphic to that of its own mirror. This self-mirror property, holding not merely classically but after the inclusion of all instanton corrections, provides a strong internal consistency check on our computation.

Furthermore, our example bears directly on a conjecture concerning the fate of torsion under mirror symmetry. It has been proposed that mirror symmetry should exchange the torsion subgroups of the second and fourth cohomology (or, dually, homology) groups of a mirror pair, in a manner analogous to the exchange of Hodge numbers. Previous evidence for this conjecture came largely from toric constructions. The threefold X studied here is decidedly non-toric, and our findings furnish the first non-toric example supporting the conjectured exchange of torsion subgroups between mirror manifolds. In doing so, this work extends the reach of the conjecture beyond the toric setting and deepens our understanding of how discrete topological data behave under the mirror correspondence.

## Conclusion

By combining mirror symmetry with an explicit B-model analysis on the mirror of a Calabi-Yau threefold equipped with Z₃ × Z₃ Wilson lines and homological torsion, we have computed the complete prepotential and extracted instanton numbers that, for the first time, depend on the torsion part of the curve's homology class. This result establishes the quantum self-mirror nature of X and provides a novel non-toric confirmation of the conjectured exchange of torsion subgroups under mirror symmetry, opening a new avenue for the study of discrete structures in the enumerative geometry of Calabi-Yau manifolds.

**Abstract**

Mirror symmetry has long been conjectured to exchange the torsion subgroups of the integral cohomology of a Calabi–Yau threefold $X$ and its mirror $\hat{X}$—concretely, interchanging $\mathrm{Tor}\, H^{2}(X,\mathbb{Z})$ with $\mathrm{Tor}\, H^{3}(\hat{X},\mathbb{Z})$ and vice versa. While this exchange has been verified in several toric complete-intersection and Batyrev–Borisov constructions, examples outside the toric framework have remained scarce, leaving open the question of how robust the phenomenon is once one departs from combinatorial reflexive-polytope data. In this work we present an explicitly constructed non-toric mirror pair realized as a free quotient of a complete intersection in a product of Grassmannians, whose defining data does not arise from any nef-partition of a reflexive polytope. Using a combination of homological Perron–Frobenius techniques, a determination of the fundamental group from the acting quotient, and a computation of the Brauer group via the Bockstein and universal-coefficient sequences, we show that $X$ carries $\mathrm{Tor}\,H^{2}(X,\mathbb{Z}) \cong \mathbb{Z}_{k}$ with trivial $H^{3}$-torsion, while its mirror $\hat{X}$ exhibits precisely the reciprocal pattern, $\mathrm{Tor}\,H^{3}(\hat{X},\mathbb{Z}) \cong \mathbb{Z}_{k}$ with trivial $H^{2}$-torsion. We interpret this result physically as the interchange of a discrete gauge symmetry (a torsional $B$-field, valued in the Brauer group) with a discrete flux/Wilson-line structure under the $T$-duality underlying the SYZ picture, matching the expected action on the associated discrete charge lattices. The example thereby provides the first non-toric confirmation of the conjectured torsion exchange and suggests that the phenomenon reflects an intrinsic feature of mirror symmetry rather than an artifact of toric constructions. We comment on implications for the completeness of the discrete data specifying a Calabi–Yau string compactification and on obstructions to extending the analysis to genuinely non-abelian torsion.
